claim_vs_prior_implication.evidence: Meyer-Schmidt DSS-19 computes det(dW/dz)(a,m) in mutual-distance+multiplier coordinates, nonzero for all positive m except m*=(13+11*sqrt2)/12 approx 2.3797, with nullity 2 and two eigenvalues changing sign at m*, and constructs local kite (m>m*) and trapezoid (m<m*) branches via Liapunov-Schmidt. The draft's transverse-zero formula gives nu*=(84-36*sqrt2)/(25+38*sqrt2), i.e. mu*=1/nu*=(13+11*sqrt2)/12 identically (verified numerically to 1e-15), so the degeneracy locus coincides. DSS-19 therefore implies nondegeneracy at every m != m*, hence on [1,2], as a corollary. It does NOT compute Hessian eigenvalue signs or Morse indices on [1,2]: it states only nullity 2 and sign change at m*, without resolving which side is definite, and its determinant is in different (distance/multiplier) coordinates, not a transverse-Hessian inertia certificate. The submitted headline's new content is exactly that missing inertia: closed-form even/odd blocks, commuting-block Schur identity, factored Z=2(4nu+1)L(nu)/nu with L affine increasing and L(1/2)>0, yielding uniform PD and index 0 at both endpoints and degree contribution +1. Nondegeneracy alone does not supply the index; the index plus uniform PD does not follow by lookup from DSS-19. Local kite/trapezoid existence near m* does not contradict the headline, which forbids only branching points in (1,2), consistent with DSS-19's unique degeneracy at ~2.38 outside [1,2].
